newsitem.title: GERMANY: German official oilseed area forecast seen high.
newsitem.headline: German official oilseed area forecast seen high.

text.p: The official projection for Germany's 1997 oilseeds acreage appears to be on the high side, both the ZMP farm price and marketing office and an influential broker said.
The Bonn farm ministry on Monday said the oilseeds area for both food and industrial uses may be expanded to just over one million hectares, 15 percent above last year's figure.
Rapeseed would be roughly one million ha (854,000 ha 1996) and sunseed 30,000 ha (44,000).
But ZMP's weekly grains and oilseeds report said the figure was "unexpectedly high" and noted a recent private forecast, which had been reliable last year, was much lower.

The survey from the Union for the Promotion of Oil and Protein Crops (Ufop) earlier this month said farmers intended to plant 740,640 ha to food uses. It since added 124,173 ha for industrial purposes, giving a total 864,813 ha.
Rapeseed for food use accounted for 708,817 ha (681,000 winter plantings and possibly 27,817 spring).
A total 122,135 ha of non-food rapeseed plantings consisted of an estimated 119,000 ha in the winter and a projected 3,135 ha in the spring.
UFOP stood by its survey which was based on a telephone poll of farms known to be oilseeds-intensive, a spokesman said.
Authorised Matif broker Juergen Kiefer in Norheim said the winter rapeseed figures from UFOP looked more precise because they were backed by indications from seed suppliers.
The winter rapeseed area was restricted by late grain harvesting in 1996, which hampered early winter rape plantings, and high wheat prices. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
